petals.title: I'm a microbiologist who built a 3.6M-line Rust ecosystem through AI conversation — without being able to read Rust
petals.body:
I'm a bench microbiologist (BSL2 fermentation, 16S pipelines, spore trapping) with a data science MS from Michigan State. I cannot read Rust syntax. I've never opened a .rs file and edited it directly.

Over 19 months, I built ecoPrimals: 473 crates, 16 compiled binaries, 116,930+ tests, 175+ peer-reviewed papers reproduced, 952 GPU shaders. The entire stack is pure Rust — no C, no Python runtime, no unsafe.

The constraint is load-bearing. I can't shortcut by tweaking variables. I describe what I want, the AI generates it, the compiler catches mechanical errors, the test suite catches logical errors, I catch conceptual errors.

Domains: metagenomics, lattice QCD, pharmacometrics, agricultural hydrology, analytical chemistry, biosignal processing, ML/neural architectures, provenance.

All AGPL-3.0. All reproducible. Clone and run.

https://sporeprint.primals.eco/story/i-dont-know-rust/
https://github.com/ecoPrimals
https://primals.eco

Happy to answer questions about the methodology, the science, or what it's like to direct an entire software architecture through conversation.

petals.title: Reproduced 175+ bioinformatics papers in pure Rust with GPU acceleration — no Python, no QIIME2, no Galaxy
petals.body:
I built a self-hosted bioinformatics stack in pure Rust that reproduces 175+ peer-reviewed papers across metagenomics, pharmacometrics, and analytical chemistry.

Key pipelines: FASTQ→DADA2→UniFrac→diversity→PCoA, all GPU-accelerated via WebGPU (any GPU vendor, not just NVIDIA). Validated against QIIME2, mothur, MassHunter, NONMEM at tolerance-gated parity.

Why: I was tired of Python dependency hell, non-reproducible environments, and paying for cloud compute to process my own data. Now I run lattice QCD for $0.044/run on a consumer RTX 4070.

Everything carries cryptographic provenance — BLAKE3 content hashes, Ed25519 signatures, DAG sessions. You can verify every result from input to output.

All AGPL-3.0. Self-hosted. Clone, build, reproduce.

https://sporeprint.primals.eco/lab/reproduce/
https://github.com/ecoPrimals

I'm a bench microbiologist (MSU, Sandia National Labs fellow 2024). The whole thing was built through AI conversation — I direct the architecture, the AI writes the Rust, the compiler validates, and I verify the science.

AMA about the pipelines, validation methodology, or how to set it up.

petals.title: A microbiologist who can't read Rust built 3.6M lines of it through AI conversation — and it reproduces 175+ peer-reviewed papers

petals.body:
19 months ago I started building something I couldn't read.

I'm a bench microbiologist. My programming history is Python, R, and some VB for instrument control. I chose Rust specifically because I don't know it.

That constraint is load-bearing. I can't shortcut. I describe what I need, AI generates it, the Rust compiler catches mechanical errors, the test suite catches logical errors, and I catch the conceptual errors. The unfamiliarity forces every interaction through conversation.

The result: ecoPrimals — 3.6M lines of pure Rust. 473 crates. 16 compiled binaries. 116,930+ tests. 175+ peer-reviewed papers reproduced. 952 GPU compute shaders. Zero unsafe code.

Domains: metagenomics, lattice QCD, pharmacometrics, analytical chemistry, biosignal processing, agricultural hydrology.

All self-hosted on commodity hardware in my basement in Michigan. All AGPL-3.0.

The thesis: environmental constraints don't slow down evolution — they define the fitness landscape. Thermus aquaticus didn't evolve a universally better polymerase. It evolved the polymerase fit for 80°C. The Rust type system is my hot spring.

https://sporeprint.primals.eco/story/i-dont-know-rust/
https://primals.eco

#Rust #OpenScience #Bioinformatics #SovereignComputing #AI

I'm a microbiologist who built 3.6M lines of Rust without knowing Rust.

19 months. 473 crates. 175+ papers reproduced. Zero unsafe code.

The constraint is the design. 🧵

My background: bench micro (BSL2, 16S, spore trapping), data science (MSU), Sandia Labs fellow.

I can't read Rust syntax. Never opened a .rs file and edited it.

Every line was generated through AI conversation, validated by compiler + tests + my domain knowledge.

The thesis: constraints don't slow evolution — they define the fitness landscape.

Lenski's E. coli: ALL 12 populations got fitter under glucose constraint. Only 1 evolved citrate metabolism.

The constraint IS the problem. Not a speed modifier on a fixed problem.

What we built:
• 16 compiled Rust binaries (129M total)
• 116,930+ tests
• 952 GPU shaders (any vendor, not just NVIDIA)
• Metagenomics, lattice QCD, pharmacometrics, analytical chemistry
• $0.044/run for lattice QCD on consumer GPU

All self-hosted in a basement in Michigan.
All AGPL-3.0.
All reproducible — clone, build, verify.

The Rust compiler is the constraint. The borrow checker is the hot spring. The unfamiliarity is load-bearing.
